name: Joash
overview: Joash was a male king of Israel and the son of Jehoahaz, as recorded in 2 Kings 13:9. His role as king places him within the line of Israelite monarchs, though specific tribal affiliation is not noted. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him in the provided information.
namesAndTitles: The name Joash appears as a proper name without a given meaning in the provided data, referenced in 2 Kings 13:9. He is also known as Jehoash, a name meaning 'YHWH bestows' or 'man of YHWH,' indicating a connection to the Lord, as noted in 2 Kings 13:10. Additionally, he held the title 'King of Israel,' clearly identifying his royal office (2 Kings 13:14).
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Joash as the son of Jehoahaz (2 Kings 13:9). It is also inferred that Jeroboam was his father according to 2 Kings 14:16, suggesting a dynastic lineage. Beyond these relationships, no further family details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Joash's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his role as king of Israel, continuing the monarchy through his lineage as the son of Jehoahaz. His reign contributes to the unfolding history of Israel's leadership during a period documented in the books of Kings. His dual naming as Joash and Jehoash reflects the common biblical practice of variant name forms, with the latter emphasizing divine association. His place in the royal succession underscores God's providential governance over Israel's history.
